messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/generate (p99 > 1s) — paging @maya, @sam, @olga. Streaming stalls and tail spikes starting 1950001200. Auto-run diagnostics kicked off. :rotating_light:

maya: got the page, looking. p95 jumped from ~120ms to 420ms, p99 ~1.1s from metrics. Is customer impact confirmed?

sam: yes, seeing increased retry rates from clients and a couple of 5xx errors that correlate with the latency window. Chart: /dashboards/latency?svc=inference&range=30m (linked)

olga: logs show lots of KV cache evictions around the same time. Eviction spikes -> prefill failing to keep hot prefixes in cache. suspect fragmentation + decode-prefill imbalance on the new routing policy rollout.

pj: repro logs from a worker: ```
[2026-03-14T02:11:58Z] host=gpu-12 tail_lat=1350ms p95=480ms p99=1180ms evictions=4823 kv_prefill_rate=0.12 decode_rate=0.85
[2026-03-14T02:12:05Z] model=rw-v2 shard=3 cache_frag_pct=72 cache_items=1.2M
```

maya: good data. olga, can you confirm which pool is hit (dedicated vs hosted)?

olga: looks like mix, but majority on dedicated pool kp-3 in us-west2 where we deployed the new kernel selector yesterday. Hostnames: kp-3-{10..14}. Prefill tasks are getting preempted by decode under burst workload.

sam: mitigation options: 1) temporarily disable new kernel selector rollouts for kp-3, 2) bump prefill concurrency, 3) enable fallback routing to smaller model variant to reduce cache pressure. Thoughts?

pj: quick and safe: add a transient routing rule -> route 30% of traffic off kp-3 to fallback pool (kp-burst) and increase cache.prefill_ratio. Command I propose: ```sh
redwoodctl route update --svc inference --rule "if pool==kp-3 then weight=70 else weight=30" && redwoodctl set config inference.cache.prefill_ratio=0.6 --target kp-3
```

maya: let's do routing + prefill bump first. pj, run the route change and set prefill, but keep change small and watch. sam, watch SLOs and errors channel. olga, collect heap/cached item histograms for kp-3.

deploy-bot: deploy job #37129 started: apply-routing-rules -> kp-3 (user=pj). ETA ~20s.

pj: applied route change and prefill config. Paste of commands & responses: ```
> redwoodctl route update --svc inference --rule "pool:kep=kp-3 => weight=70; otherwise => weight=30"
OK: routes updated (commit 37129)
> redwoodctl set config inference.cache.prefill_ratio=0.6 --target kp-3
OK: config queued (commit 37130)
```

maya: seeing initial drop in p99 to ~820ms, p95 to ~300ms. still above target but improving. evictions down 40% on kp-3. :+1:

sam: errors reduced. However streaming stalls remain for some long-lived sessions — likely due to cache fragmentation causing uneven KV lookup times (single hot prefixes missing). Need to run controlled prefill for those hot prefixes.

olga: I can push a targeted prefill for top 100 prefixes hitting tail latency: `rbctl prefill --pool kp-3 --prefix-file /tmp/top_prefixes.txt --batch-size 64`. Will run low impact job.

pj: go for it. Also suggest enabling the temporary per-shard eviction threshold: `inference.runtime.cache.eviction_threshold=0.85` to avoid mass evictions.

olga: prefill job started. Logs: ```
[2026-03-14T02:16:45Z] prefill:start prefixes=100 pool=kp-3 batch=64
[2026-03-14T02:17:30Z] prefill:progress 60% warmed=62
[2026-03-14T02:18:15Z] prefill:complete warmed=100 duration=90s
```

maya: after prefill p99 ~560ms, p95 ~210ms. streaming stalls dropping. This looks like KV pressure + fragmentation root cause. Need postmortem and longer-term fix (adaptive prefill, stricter eviction policies, monitor per-prefix miss rate).

sam: I'm drafting an incident notice (low customer impact now but breached SLO). Will include timeline, mitigation steps, and customer impact assessment.

pj: schedule a follow-up with runtime team to revert kernel selector changes or tune it — that rollout likely lowered prefill priority.

deploy-bot: commit 37129/37130 applied successfully.

maya: handing to night oncall @oncall-night for observability follow-up & postmortem tracking. Summary: transient p99 SLO breach driven by KV cache evictions/fragmentation after recent kernel selector rollout; mitigations: route 30% off kp-3, bump prefill_ratio, targeted prefill of hot prefixes, adjusted eviction threshold.

oncall-night: acknowledged, I have the runbook and will own the writeup. Adding action items: 1) rollback or tune kernel selector on kp-3; 2) add per-prefix miss rate alert; 3) automate targeted prefill for top N prefixes.

maya: thanks team. closing paging loop — will convert this thread into incident record. :white_check_mark:
